title: Stability layer for attention kernels and adaptive decode throttling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last two quarters we have seen intermittent P95/P99 latency spikes and subtle throughput regressions during model startup and during mixed-workload bursts. Root cause signals point to instability when the kernel selector flips between FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants under certain sequence-length and head-config distributions, combined with decode-side jitter caused by microbatch churn.

Goal: Build a lightweight "stability layer" that sits above the kernel selection heuristic to: 1) detect oscillatory kernel flips at runtime, 2) apply soft-fallbacks (grace periods and bandwidth-limited trials) to avoid thrashing, and 3) coordinate with an adaptive decode throttler that smooths microbatch ingress to maintain latency SLOs without a large cost increase.

Non-goals: We are not replacing the kernel autotuner or doing full model retraining. This ticket focuses on runtime orchestration, safeguards, and targeted experiments.

Success metrics (baseline vs experiment):
- Reduce P99 token latency spikes during startup and bursts by >= 30%
- Keep mean throughput within 95% of baseline for steady-state workloads
- Reduce kernel-selection flip rate (v2<->v3) on affected models by >= 75%
- No increase in model error rate or artifact generation (sanity evals)

Proposed approach:
1) Detection: implement a lightweight flip-detector that maintains a sliding window of kernel decisions, per model-version and per node, and signals when flips exceed a configurable threshold.
2) Stability policy: when a flip is detected, mark the model/node with a soft-stable candidate for a configurable grace period (e.g., 15s) where the runtime prefers the current kernel and only allows probes at a reduced cadence.
3) Adaptive decode throttler: implement a token-bucket-based shaping layer between request admission and decode scheduling that reduces decode-side microbatch churn for models exhibiting startup jitter. Throttler parameters are per-model and can be tuned by the advisor service.
4) Coordinated rollout: tie the stability layer to rollout policies so that canary variants get stricter probe budgets, and Dedicated/Private installations can opt-in to more aggressive throttling.
5) Observability: add metrics and dashboards for flip-rate, grace-period activations, throttler utilization, and decode-latency histograms. Emit an event stream for post-mortem analysis.

Experiment matrix and tests:
- Controlled lab: synthetic workload matrix across sequence lengths [64,128,512], head configs [8,16], and batch sizes [1,4,8] to measure flip-rate reduction and latency impact.
- Canary: 5% traffic on staging with runtime-1.22 and adaptive throttler enabled for model group alpha-llama-30k. Monitor for 48 hours.
- Stress: bursty arrival patterns using production traces to validate that throttler smooths microbatch formation without causing timeouts.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement flip-detector + metrics + unit tests (this ticket).
- Phase 2 (lab): integrate stability policy + throttler; run matrix above and collect baselines.
- Phase 3 (canary): circuit-breaker guarded canary rollout on staging; revert on regression.
- Phase 4 (prod): gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with telemetry gating.

Rollback criteria:
- Any sustained (>10min) increase in P50/P95 latency by >10% or P99 by >5% versus baseline during canary.
- Throughput drop leading to queued requests beyond configured SLOs.
- Increase in kernel-selection errors or decode failures.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Conservative grace periods prevent rapid adaptation; we need to tune to avoid masking legitimate better kernels.
- Throttling smooths jitter but may slightly increase mean latency on innocuous tails; accept small mean increases if tail improves.
- Per-model tuning increases config surface; plan to surface advisor recommendations in Console.

Open questions:
- Default grace period and probe cadence for v2/v3 trials? Proposed starting point: 15s grace, probe every 5s at low sampling rate.
- How to surface costs of throttling in the Console cost breakdown? Product/PM input needed.

Links and artifacts:
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/runtime/flip-detector-2025
- Proposal doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/confluence/runtime/stability-layer-design
- Experiment harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1245

Deliverables:
- Flip-detector library and tests
- Stability policy controller and configuration knobs
- Adaptive decode-throttler component with per-model configs
- Dashboards and alerting rules for regressions
- Canary runbook and automation (rollback hooks)
